text:
Priya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a few edge-case questions about the review/promo window we didn't get to. Can @Alex or @Jordan clarify?

Alex (People Ops): Yep — dropping in. Ask away. :wave:

Priya: Thanks! 1) What happens if someone was on LOA during the review window but their manager still wants to consider them for an off-cycle promotion?

Jordan (People Ops): Good one. Short answer: managers can nominate for an off-cycle, but it requires an exception request and calibration committee approval. We need the nominee's recent work summary + rationale.

Sam: How much backdating is allowed if approved? For comp adjustments/merit bump timing?

Alex (People Ops): We avoid retroactive base pay more than one pay cycle prior to approval. For fairness, we typically apply increases in the next payroll. If it's a comp correction, we can do retro pay but it'll be treated as a one-time lump adjustment and routed to finance.

Maya: If someone had a performance improvement plan (PIP) that closed successfully during the window, are they eligible for promotion immediately?

Jordan (People Ops): Promotions after PIP closure are considered, but require a strong narrative from the manager and an extra level of calibration review. We want to ensure sustainable improvement.

Carlos: Cross-functional note: what if someone rotates teams mid-window? Which manager owns the promo decision?

Alex (People Ops): Owning manager is whoever has official manager-of-record on the last day of the review window. If rotation happens inside the window, best practice is manager-to-manager handoff doc and joint nomination.

Lia: A benefits question — someone asked about eligibility for parental leave if the resource was hired within 30 days before the window and then goes on leave during the review period. Does that affect comp/bonus eligibility?

Jordan (People Ops): Parental leave eligibility follows our benefits policy (service-based), not the review timeline. Bonus eligibility is tied to employment status on payout date and manager recommendations. We won't exclude solely for timing, but payout/proration rules can apply.

Priya: Can you paste the exception request template? I missed it earlier.

PeopleOpsBot: Exception request form: https://internal.redwood/peopleops/exception-request || Required: nominee name, manager, reason, evidence (projects/metrics), requested outcome, finance impact estimate.

Sam: For calibration, will ICs get visibility into their calibration cohort/anchors? Or is it manager-only?

Alex (People Ops): Calibration discussions are manager-only. We will publish cohort-level band movement summaries after cycles (no names) so folks can see macro decisions and band changes.

Maya: If a promotion is approved but the manager wants a different effective date (defer one month for project continuity), is that allowed?

Jordan (People Ops): Yes, with manager justification. The effective date should be within 60 days of approval unless there's a compelling operational reason. Compensation/proration will be documented.

Carlos: Edge: someone onboarded via contractor-to-FTE conversion during the window. Do we treat their start date from contractor period for leveling/tenure questions?

Alex (People Ops): We evaluate case-by-case. Typically FTE start date governs benefits and band eligibility, but prior contractor work can be used in the promotion narrative. Manager should note previous deliverables in the packet.

Priya: Awesome, super helpful. One last: can we get a short FAQ doc for managers that covers these 6 points?

Jordan (People Ops): On it. We'll publish a 1-page "Review Window Manager FAQ" by EOD tomorrow and drop in #people-ops.

Lia: Thanks team! :pray:

Alex (People Ops): Thanks all — feel free to DM if you have specific edge cases.

PeopleOpsBot: Reminder: review packet deadline in 5 days. Uploads must go through the portal: https://internal.redwood/peopleops/packets
